about: On the session entity of a creation, respec or change-appearance session: NetId and two more values. Script Extender: CCSessionCommon.

evidence.says: Script Extender declares eoc::character_creation::SessionCommonComponent::NetId at +0x0 (BG3Extender/GameDefinitions/Components/CharacterCreation.h:166): its author's name and type; the offset is computed from the declared types. Not checked against the game's code.

Script Extender declares eoc::character_creation::SessionCommonComponent::field_4 at +0x4 (BG3Extender/GameDefinitions/Components/CharacterCreation.h:166): its author's name and type; the offset is computed from the declared types; the computed offset equals the one in its earlier name. Not checked against the game's code.

Script Extender declares eoc::character_creation::SessionCommonComponent::field_8 at +0x8 (BG3Extender/GameDefinitions/Components/CharacterCreation.h:166): its author's name and type; the offset is computed from the declared types; the computed offset equals the one in its earlier name. the game's executable keeps this type name among its ECS type names (gatekit symbols types)

in a change-appearance session (Osi.StartChangeAppearance on the host of a running level) one entity carries it with ServerCCSessionOwner and CCDefinitionChangeAppearance; NetId reads 65537, the same number as the owner's UserId; the two other members read 0

survey.from: Script Extender's declarations (BG3Extender/GameDefinitions/Components/CharacterCreation.h:166, kind component), by gatekit symbols se-layouts on 2026-11-14
survey.names: Every name here is Script Extender's author's (his headers), not the game's own: they are kept because they are what the extender's Lua answers to and what bg3_verify compares, and every field carries the rung `extender` - the extender's name for the field at that offset, which nobody has checked against the game's code. A name is raised from `extender` only with evidence from the code, by `gatekit names set`.
